caption: R7 000 a month toward lobola on top of what I send my parents. Anyone else saving for two futures at once?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R38 700
p/m salary
Living in Kathu
slides.body:
Male, 33
Single, saving toward lobola for his fiancée
Job: Mine control room operator
Net salary: R38 700 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Company-linked flat, top-up over the housing allowance
slides.body: Cheaper than town rent, still not free.

slides.title: Lobola savings
slides.includes: Into a separate account, talks with her family started this year
slides.body: It's the biggest thing I've ever saved toward on purpose.

slides.title: Parents' support
slides.includes: My parents' electricity, groceries top-up, my youngest brother's school fees
slides.body: Nobody asked me to take this on in writing. I just started, and it's not going anywhere.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Needed for the drive out to the mine gate every shift.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Big shop plus the extra when I'm cooking for my parents' visit
slides.body: It stretches further than it used to, which tells you something about the rest of this list.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, insurance, phone & data, funeral policies for both households, a stokvel with the guys from shift, savings for the wedding itself
slides.body: Sixteen thousand seven hundred rand of things running at once, on top of the lobola and my parents.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 700. Saving for two futures — my parents' and my own wedding — at the same time is the part nobody warns you about.

slides.title: I stopped losing track of what I'm actually saving for
slides.body:
I've got the lobola savings as its own goal in Beyond Horizon, separate from my parents' support and my everyday spending.

Seeing them as three different lines instead of one blur made the number feel possible instead of endless.

No bank login needed.
